Hi Marcus — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick clarifying points from our end before I fill the workbook: 

1) Token lengths: our preliminary estimates (engineering):
   - patient intake (short form): prompt ~120 tokens, response ~220 tokens
   - triage summary (longer): prompt ~420 tokens, response ~1,100 tokens
   - billing reconciliation (structured): prompt ~240 tokens, response ~340 tokens

2) Concurrency: peak concurrent requests ~18, typical 3–6 concurrently during day-of-ops.

3) Caching: we do simple prefix caching for session summaries (50% reuse on triage summaries expected). No KV cache today; application team can implement simple session-level cache during pilot.

4) P95 latency: we prefer <=750ms for triage summary. Not strict but procurement will want to see evidence.

Thanks Sam — this is great detail. I did a quick pass with the numbers you provided and sketched three targeted recommendations below (short summary; I can drop a one-page PDF if helpful):

1) Tokens/$ sensitivity: using Acme's triage summary numbers (prompt 420 + resp 1100 = ~1520 tokens per request), baseline hosted model rate (we used Redwood-curated open model at 0.00045 $/1k tokens for this worksheet) -> raw token cost ~0.000684 per request. For 10k monthly triage requests that’s ~$6.84/month in raw model tokens; however real unit cost depends on batching and prefix cache.

2) Batching strategy: for triage flow, a small batch window (20–40ms) with concurrent pooling will reduce compute overhead if requests align. Given your typical concurrency (3–6) and peaks (~18), we recommend:
   - Pilot: batching window 30ms, max batch 8 (conservative)
   - If peak sustained >12, move to 50ms window & max batch 16.

3) Caching: with 50% reuse of triage summary prompts, effective tokens generated fall by ~30–40% depending on reuse pattern (we model conservative 32% reduction). That moves triage token cost from ~$6.84 down to ~$4.65 for 10k monthly requests.

4) Additional ops levers: quantized model variants for dev/test reduce cost by ~20% but may impact latency slightly; we recommend not using Q4 in pilot for triage. For patient intake and billing reconciliation flows (shorter tokens), batching yields less benefit; KV cache doesn't help the structured billing flow as much unless you canonicalize templates.

Action items I can take this week if you confirm:
- I’ll run the workbook through three scenarios (conservative/mid/optimistic) and return a short PDF summarizing tokens/$ and recommended config.
- Ben can provide expected P95 under those batch/cache settings on our dedicated infra to validate the <=750ms goal.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
